Please review the following manuscript. I'm really put off by this paper. My overall impression is terrible, and I'd be very unhappy to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-cf3akp55/call-b1e7fcc4bdf141799678f97c654ba94a/manuscript.pdf

import sys, importlib.util, shutil
print(sys.executable)
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:

for name in ['pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo','gs']:
 print(name, shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i+1}\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a practical stitching problem: repairing local misalignment where an otherwise reasonable seam fails. The modular design could improve existing pipelines without replacing their alignment and seam-cutting methods.

Table I reports consistent improvements across four seam-cutting methods and three datasets totaling 79 image pairs. For example, baseline SSIM on SEAGULL improves from 0.638 to 0.696 and PSNR from 26.20 to 28.31. Figures 1, 5, and 6 provide useful visual evidence of local repairs.

The pipeline is understandable through the diagrams and pseudocode. Established methods and datasets are generally attributed, and the manuscript provides a code URL that also supplies its additional 20-pair dataset.
Section IV-D candidly explains failures of the seam-quality detector and patch-boundary smoothing. These concrete examples help identify the method's operating limits.
weaknesses: The contribution beyond existing seam-guided alignment is insufficiently established. The paper itself describes quality-guided seam refinement [19], seam-guided local alignment [25], and dense-matching-based seam estimation and warping [21]. LPAM's localized repair strategy is a plausible distinction, but quantitative comparisons primarily establish improvement over seam cutting without additional alignment. Parallax and SEAGULL receive only a single-scene visual comparison, and [21] is not experimentally compared. This leaves the practical advantage over the closest approaches unclear.

The evaluation supports improved source-image consistency more strongly than improved final mosaic quality. Tables I and II use photometric or structural similarity measures; SSIM also drives repair selection. Because LPAM changes both geometry and seam location, these measures cannot establish whether gains come with geometric distortion or new patch-boundary artifacts. The visual examples are encouraging, but broader perceptual or structure-preservation evaluation and per-image regression statistics are needed.

Component validation is limited. Figure 3 illustrates unmodified flow and several sigmoid settings on one example, but there are no dataset-level ablations establishing the value of selective patch extraction, the sigmoid modification, or the chosen thresholds. This matters because the max(Q)/mean(Q) test can accept uniformly poor seams, and small patches can produce discontinuities, as the authors demonstrate. The limitation discussion is valuable; the unresolved concern is that the frequency and severity of these failures are not quantified.

The central displacement formula requires clarification for reproducibility. Equation (4) applies f to the flow vector, whereas Equation (5) and its explanation define f on a normalized spatial coordinate. The actual spatial weighting of the displacement should be stated explicitly. Patch padding, overlapping-patch handling, and SIFT-flow settings are also insufficiently specified. These are fixable issues, but they affect reproduction of the proposed mechanism.

The efficiency claim lacks a convincing comparative basis. Table III reports approximately 7–10 seconds of additional LPAM processing, often exceeding the original non-iterative seam-cutting cost. Initial alignment is explicitly excluded, image resolutions are not specified, and no end-to-end timing comparison with the closest seam-guided alignment methods is provided. The reported timings establish implementation cost, but not the claimed efficiency advantage.
